atlas-tw.0058: At the NTU fair of 7 March 2026, 70% of the 347 companies offered cross-disciplinary roles, and TSMC’s own campus drive lists business and accounting among the majors it recruits, next to engineering and computer science.
atlas-tw.0059: TSMC planned to hire around 8,000 engineers and technicians in 2026 and offered master’s-level new hires an average of NT$2.2 million a year; it recruits through campus fairs at National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University and Taipei Tech, and its summer internship prefers master’s and PhD students.
atlas-tw.0060: Employers recruit at named campuses: the 2017 financial-group fairs were at National Taiwan University (5 March), Tsinghua (18 March) and National Chengchi University (24 March), and TSMC’s 2026 visits listed National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University and Taipei Tech.
atlas-tw.0061: For the work permit, graduates of the top 200 universities can use a streamlined application for specialised professional work, according to NTU’s international office; the criteria are on the EZ Work Taiwan portal.
atlas-tw.0062: The NTU campus fair “VISION 2026” on 7 March 2026 is the largest in the year, with 347 companies and 450 booths; TSMC also holds information sessions, in person or online, which students register for on the university’s site.
atlas-tw.0063: The financial groups’ management-associate fairs ran in March in the 2017 season, at three universities within three weeks (5, 18 and 24 March).
atlas-tw.0064: A spring peak of campus fairs (NTU on 7 March 2026) and application windows that close in April and May (TSMC campus recruitment 30 April, internship 8 May), with online portals carrying openings through the year.
atlas-tw.0065: New entrants with a graduate degree earned NT$52,000 a month on average in 2024, against NT$34,000 for university graduates; TSMC’s summer internship prefers master’s and PhD students, and master’s-level new hires averaged NT$2.2 million a year.
atlas-tw.0066: No recognition centre screens degrees for ordinary jobs. For the work permit the employer files the degree with the Workforce Development Agency, which reads a master’s as needing no experience and a bachelor’s as needing two years; a degree from a top-1,500 university waives the experience.
atlas-tw.0067: Recruiters go to named campuses (NTU, Tsinghua, Chengchi, Taiwan Normal, Taipei Tech) and the work-permit rules favour top-200 universities, but no page we read says how far the university name decides who is interviewed.
atlas-tw.0068: University graduates reach employers through campus recruiting, internships and portals; apprenticeship or dual-study contracts are not a route we found in any source for university graduates.
atlas-tw.0069: We found no page on public-sector graduate hiring in Taiwan; the sources read describe private employers (TSMC, financial groups, the Big Four) as the graduate route, so we rate the public sector small for a foreign graduate.
atlas-tw.0070: The ordinary work permit needs NT$47,971 a month in pay, and the sponsor needs paid-in capital of at least NT$5 million if under a year old or turnover of at least NT$10 million; science-park firms and certified innovative start-ups are exempt from the size tests. Taiwanese-degree graduates score on a points test instead, with no salary floor. The rules themselves are under Visas.
atlas-tw.0071: A photo is common on Taiwanese résumés, in our reading; the Taiwanese interview can also touch on family and private life, which GTAI says is not taboo.
atlas-tw.0072: Applicants usually submit a CV and a cover letter, often through a portal’s structured résumé. We found no page that sets a length; treat two pages as our reading.
atlas-tw.0073: GTAI says applicants usually submit a cover letter with the CV, then are invited to interviews.
atlas-tw.0074: Unlike in Germany, employers rarely ask for references or former employers, according to GTAI.
atlas-tw.0075: For a work permit the employer files the degree, and the Admetia library notes that Italian diplomas go through the consular legalisation chain of the Taipei office in Rome or Milan, not an apostille.
atlas-tw.0076: Taiwanese résumé forms usually include an expected-salary field, in our reading; pay is the top incentive at every level, according to GTAI.
atlas-tw.0077: No page we read says how routine background or reference checks are; GTAI says employers rarely ask for references.
atlas-tw.0078: Portals and campus drives take applications directly, and LINE is used to schedule interviews; we found no page showing referrals as the main door.
atlas-tw.0079: A foreigner abroad needs an employer that files for the work permit, with NT$47,971 a month in pay and two years of experience for a bachelor’s; Taiwanese-degree graduates have a two-year permit-free job-seeking stay that applicants from abroad do not.
atlas-tw.0080: Chinese counts for up to 30 of the 70 points in the graduate points test, and many positions require it; German companies look for staff who at least communicate in English, though graduates’ English is often passive. English-only roles are mostly in semiconductor engineering and foreign firms.
atlas-tw.0081: GTAI describes the usual sequence as a CV and cover letter, then interviews, mostly in person; technical tests, sales presentations and panel rounds are typical next steps, and companies use LINE to arrange them.
atlas-tw.0082: TSMC’s campus process is an online application on its portal, then interviews for shortlisted candidates: in 2026 applications ran to 30 April and interviews to 30 June, about two months. For the summer internship, applications ran to 8 May and interviews to 29 May.
atlas-tw.0083: Interviewers may ask about family members and family planning, which GTAI says is not taboo in Taiwan; phone and online interviews are less common than in-person ones.
atlas-tw.0084: The management-associate tracks at financial groups were quoted with English-test floors in 2017: TOEIC 750 at SinoPac and TOEIC 900 at First Bank.
atlas-tw.0085: After three months of service an employer ending a contract under the Labor Standards Act must give 10 days’ notice up to one year of service, 20 days from one to three years and 30 days after three years, or pay wages for the notice period. Severance is one month’s average wage per year of service, and a worker may take paid time off to look for a job during the notice period.
atlas-tw.0086: Entry pay is modest and uniform: new entrants averaged NT$37,000 a month in 2024, and 18.7% started at the basic wage of NT$27,470 (19.7% of university graduates and 3.5% of graduate-school graduates).
atlas-tw.0087: Among 2023 entrants still employed in December 2024, about 80% of the cohort, average pay had risen 15.7% in a year, from NT$36,000 to NT$42,000.
atlas-tw.0088: A foreign employee is enrolled in the National Health Insurance from the first day of work, the employer arranging it.
atlas-tw.0089: The sponsoring company must meet size tests: paid-in capital of at least NT$5 million if under a year old, or average turnover of at least NT$10 million, with science-park firms and certified innovative start-ups exempt. A start-up that does not meet them is rejected automatically.
atlas-tw.0090: The employer files on the EZ Work Taiwan portal with the contract, the degree and references; the work permit takes 7 to 10 working days and the whole route four to six weeks. Offer the employer a candidate who meets the NT$47,971 floor, or who is a Taiwanese-degree graduate scoring 70 points.
atlas-tw.0091: What an employer wants to hear is Mandarin ability (the points test gives 30 points for C2, 25 for B2 and 20 for B1 on the TOCFL) and a salary at or above NT$47,971, which scores 40 points.
atlas-tw.0092: TSMC and the Big Four hire many graduates but we found no page saying they sponsor foreigners from abroad; the Taiwanese-degree route (two permit-free years, then the points test) is the documented one.
atlas-tw.0093: 104 Job Bank is the standard platform; 1111 Job Bank, 518 Job Bank and Yes123 are the other local boards; LinkedIn, Cake.me and Yourator serve international and multilingual roles; the German Business Office (AHK Taiwan) posts job ads on its website.
atlas-tw.0094: The Workforce Development Agency runs the Taiwan Job Bank (the 台灣就業通 service), with job-scam warnings, in Chinese only; Talent Taiwan is the one-stop portal for foreign talent that NTU points to.
atlas-tw.0095: TSMC’s portal for campus recruitment and summer internships, with registration for its information sessions on the university’s site; the NTU campus fair in March; and your university’s career centre.
atlas-tw.0096: For work permits, the EZ Work Taiwan portal of the Workforce Development Agency, where the employer files.
atlas-tw.0097: Waiting for the autumn. TSMC’s campus applications closed on 30 April and the internship on 8 May, and the campus fairs are in March.
atlas-tw.0098: Reading city or sector pay as entry pay. New entrants averaged NT$37,000 a month in 2024 (NT$34,000 for university graduates), far below averages quoted for Hsinchu or Taipei.
atlas-tw.0099: Taking an offer from a start-up that cannot sponsor: a company under a year old with less than NT$5 million paid-in capital is rejected for a work permit.
atlas-tw.0100: Leaving out Mandarin. Chinese carries up to 30 of the 70 points for Taiwanese-degree graduates, and many positions require it.
atlas-tw.0101: Counting on references or a formal reference check to carry the application: employers rarely ask for them, so the CV, the cover letter and the tests do the work.
atlas-tw.0102: In 2017 SinoPac’s management-associate programme required TOEIC 750 and First Bank’s TOEIC 900, alongside a Chinese-language process; those figures are from 2017.
